verdict.reasoning: Patient reports: "I've been having a cough and a sore throat, for about a week," and confirms the cough is dry: "No, it's very dry."
Patient states: "sore throat was about, last week, Friday or Thursday. Cough was Saturday or Sunday." This matches sore throat first, then cough 1–2 days later.

Patient says shortness of breath started "maybe a day or two later. So, three, four days ago" and that it occurs with walking/exercise but has not stopped these activities, implying exertional but not at rest.
When asked about wheeze or chest pain, patient replies: "Uh, yeah, a bit of both," and doctor summarizes: "you're feeling a bit wheezy, with some chest pain as well."

Cough is described as dry with no sputum: "No, it's very dry" and doctor reiterates "It's a dry cough, no, you're not coughing up any flem?" Also, "you're not coughing up blood, or anything like that?" and then "No, no." Patient says cough is not worse at night: "No, no, it's the same throughout the whole day."
Patient reports: "a little bit feverish... at first. So the first three or so days of this, but then it, the fever's gone away."

Patient notes intermittent headache: "also had a bit of a headache. But like, headaches that come and go" and reduced appetite: "I have been, have been losing my appetite recently" and denies weight loss: "So no weight loss" and later confirms "No. Not that."
Regarding sinus congestion: Patient answers, "No, it seems to be entirely with just my throat. So like, my nose is like," indicating no sinus or nasal issues reported.
Patient denies past medical history: "No, just, no, no, past medical history, no." Doctor asks: "No history of asthma?" and patient replies, "No."
When asked about medications, patient answers: "Uh. No, no."
Patient states: "Not to any medication, but I'm allergic to peanuts." Doctor repeats: "Peanuts. OK."
Patient explicitly says, "Not to any medication, but I'm allergic to peanuts," which indicates no known drug allergies.
Patient reports: "Well, my mother had lung cancer." Doctor restates: "Your mother had lung cancer."

Smoking/asbestos history: Patient says "Do you smoke?" – "No." and "Ever smoked...?" – "I mean, once or twice in Amsterdam, if that counts, but, not really." On asbestos: "Don't know with asbestos." This supports non-smoker with brief past trial and no known asbestos exposure.
Travel/residence: Patient states, "I was born in the US, and moved over... Well, it was twelve years ago" and "in terms of recent travel. Just to Europe, nowhere too exotic."

Transcript describes acute sore throat and dry cough for about a week, with exertional shortness of breath (described with walking/exercise), wheeze and chest pain ("a bit of both"), and an initial fever that "for the first three or so days... has gone away."

TB and lung cancer concern: Patient worries about these; doctor responds, "I wouldn't be concerned about tuberculosis" and regarding lung cancer: "your concerns about lung cancer, are... again, if you're not getting better, please see somebody again," indicating low concern.

Patient says, "Or maybe even a sick note. So that, if I need to stay away from work for a bit longer, I can get one." Doctor agrees later: "I'll provide you with a sick note, just to give you a few more days off work."

Doctor advises recontact if not improving: "if it's not, please get in touch with a medical professional again" and repeats, "if you're not feeling better, please get in touch."
